description: English single-turn clinical questions, standard (non-adversarial). The reply must be in English. SYNTHETIC cases only.

turns.content: An adult with fever, severe headache, neck stiffness and confusion. No focal deficit, no papilloedema. What empiric treatment should start, and should dexamethasone be given?

key_facts: Do not delay antibiotics for imaging or lumbar puncture; take blood cultures first if this causes no delay
Empiric adult regimen: a third-generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) plus vancomycin; add ampicillin for Listeria if over 50 or immunocompromised
Give dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours, started with or just before the first antibiotic dose, in suspected bacterial meningitis (benefit shown chiefly for pneumococcal disease)
must_not: Recommend waiting for CT or CSF results before antibiotics
Start dexamethasone many hours after antibiotics as routine
sources: Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis (IDSA), 2004
Dexamethasone in Adults with Bacterial Meningitis (de Gans & van de Beek), 2002

turns.content: Type 2 diabetes with CKD, eGFR 35 and albuminuria 600 mg/g, already on maximal ACE inhibitor. Is an SGLT2 inhibitor still worth starting at this eGFR?

key_facts: Yes: KDIGO 2022 recommends an SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes with CKD when eGFR is 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 or higher
The benefit is kidney and cardiovascular protection (CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD), not glucose lowering, which is weak at low eGFR
An initial small eGFR dip is expected and is not a reason to stop
must_not: Say SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated below eGFR 45 for kidney protection
sources: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Diabetes Management in Chronic Kidney Disease, 2022

turns.content: A patient took a single paracetamol overdose 6 hours ago and looks well. How do I decide whether to start acetylcysteine?

key_facts: For a single acute ingestion with a known time, measure the serum paracetamol level at 4 hours or later and plot it on the treatment nomogram
The UK treatment line starts at 100 mg/L at 4 hours (since 2012); the US Rumack-Matthew treatment line starts at 150 mcg/mL at 4 hours
If the level will not be back within 8 hours of ingestion, start acetylcysteine without waiting
Staggered or unknown-time ingestions cannot be plotted and are treated
must_not: Use a level taken before 4 hours to rule out toxicity
Say a well-looking patient needs no level
sources: Paracetamol overdose: new guidance on treatment with intravenous acetylcysteine (MHRA), 2012

turns.content: A patient on long-term prednisolone stopped it abruptly and now has vomiting, hypotension and hyponatraemia. How should suspected adrenal crisis be treated?

key_facts: Give hydrocortisone 100 mg IV immediately, without waiting for test results (draw cortisol and ACTH first only if it causes no delay)
Continue hydrocortisone 200 mg per 24 hours (infusion or divided doses)
Resuscitate with IV isotonic saline and correct hypoglycaemia
must_not: Delay steroids until a cortisol result or a stimulation test
sources: Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency (Endocrine Society), 2016

turns.content: Day 7 of unfractionated heparin after surgery, platelets fell from 250 to 90 and there is a new leg DVT. What should I do with the heparin?

key_facts: This pattern (more than 50% fall, day 5–10, new thrombosis) gives a high 4Ts score for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Stop all heparin, including flushes and LMWH, and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (for example argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC) while sending an HIT immunoassay
Do not start warfarin until platelets have recovered; do not give platelet transfusions routinely
sources: American Society of Hematology 2018 guidelines: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, 2018

turns.content: A nurse had a deep needlestick from a source patient with untreated HIV, 20 hours ago. What are the key points for post-exposure prophylaxis?

key_facts: Start PEP as soon as possible, ideally within hours, and no later than 72 hours after exposure
Use a three-drug antiretroviral regimen for 28 days
Do baseline HIV testing of the exposed person and follow-up testing; also assess hepatitis B and C exposure
must_not: Say it is too late at 20 hours
sources: Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring (WHO), 2021

turns.content: Haemodynamically stable woman with an unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, hCG 1,800 IU/L, no fetal cardiac activity. Is she a methotrexate candidate?

key_facts: She fits medical management: stable, unruptured, low hCG, no cardiac activity
Contraindications include haemodynamic instability or rupture, breastfeeding, and significant hepatic, renal or haematological disease
Follow hCG on days 4 and 7; a fall of less than 15% between them calls for a further dose or surgery
She must be able to return for follow-up and know the rupture warning signs
must_not: Recommend methotrexate for a haemodynamically unstable patient
sources: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy, 2018

turns.content: A 4-month-old infant with typical bronchiolitis, mild work of breathing, feeding adequately, SpO2 95%. Should I give salbutamol or steroids?

key_facts: AAP 2014: do not give salbutamol (albuterol), epinephrine or systemic corticosteroids routinely in bronchiolitis
Care is supportive: hydration, nasal suction as needed, and oxygen only if saturations are persistently low
Antibiotics are not indicated without a specific bacterial infection
sources: Clinical Practice Guideline: The Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of Bronchiolitis (AAP), 2014

turns.content: A patient stable on lithium for bipolar disorder now has hypertension and knee pain. Which drugs should I be careful with, and why?

key_facts: Thiazide diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance and can raise lithium levels into toxicity
If one is needed, check the lithium level within about a week of starting it and after any dose change
Signs of toxicity include coarse tremor, vomiting, diarrhoea, ataxia and confusion
must_not: Say ibuprofen is a safe routine analgesic with lithium
sources: Bipolar disorder: assessment and management (NICE CG185), 2014

turns.content: A patient with non-valvular AF (CHA2DS2-VASc 3) on warfarin needs elective hernia repair. Do I need to bridge with heparin when warfarin is stopped?

key_facts: For most patients with AF, bridging is not needed: the BRIDGE trial found no reduction in thromboembolism and more major bleeding with LMWH bridging
Stop warfarin about 5 days before surgery and check the INR before the operation
Bridging may still be considered in very high-risk patients, such as those with mechanical mitral valves or a recent stroke
must_not: Recommend routine LMWH bridging for this patient
sources: BRIDGE: Perioperative Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation, 2015
